I would like to complete this post with a further analysis of the current situation regarding the matter. I used Gemini to organise and say better my thoughts ; even if I did so, these are still my proper thoughts on the matter.

------------------------------------------------

Systemic Analysis: The Blind Spots of VRChat Moderation

VRChat's safety model relies on a siloed approach that displays major structural limits:

- The Inter-Group Vacuum: Nothing prevents groups from coordinating exclusions externally. Without an official gateway, communities resort to closed-circuit, opaque fallback solutions.

- The Burden of Self-Moderation: Heavy reliance on individual blocking tools shifts the safety burden onto the individual player. This undermines group moderators and contradicts the core mission of a professional Trust & Safety staff.

- Staff vs. Self-Regulation Ambiguity: Lacking official tools, group moderators are reduced to emergency patch-works, blurring the lines between official moderation and community initiatives.

- Time-Zone & Weekend Blind Spots: Paid staff are limited to standard working hours, whereas toxic spikes peak during evenings and weekends when concurrency is highest.

- The Workload Bottleneck: Centralized ticket handling cannot scale with platform growth, leaving countless reports unaddressed in an overloaded database.

- The Ground Gap: The system lacks active, on-the-ground presence to de-escalate conflicts early and bridge isolated groups with official safety.

Conclusion:

Ignoring these frictions will not make them disappear. Formally recognizing and structuring a Community Steward role would bridge the gap between isolated group actions and official safety, alleviating staff workload while offering a unified way to preserve the VRChat experience.

------------------------------------------------

details:
I would like to suggest a community program that I truly believe can benefit everyone in the long run: Community Stewards.

- Role & Philosophy: Stewards are here to chill and enjoy VRChat like anyone else, but carry a burning ambition to assist players whenever questions arise or situations become overwhelming. Respecting players' personal boundaries, private conflicts, and individual safety tools is paramount. They step in strictly when helpful as caring mentors—guiding users on features, settings, safety tools, reports, the website, and Discord without imposing anything—and helping de-escalate tensions calmly and constructively.

- Collaboration across the board: They genuinely enjoy collaborating with all layers of the community: regular players, group moderators, world creators, and VRChat staff members both on Discord and in-game.

- Proven track record: Stewards are selected based on their established consistency and constructive history regarding bug reports, user/avatar reports, and feedback.

- Exemplary standing: They strictly abide by VRChat’s Community Guidelines, Terms of Service, and Creator Guidelines, acting as positive role models for the community.

- No moderation powers, higher report priority: Stewards do not replace standard player safety tools and have no power to mute, kick, or ban. Instead, their value lies in mediation, education, and trusted feedback loops. Their reports carry prioritized weight, reviewed by dedicated Trust & Safety team members to ensure transparency and accountability. A private Discord space would allow them to maintain clear, two-way communication with staff when complex situations require follow-up.

Visual Identity & Emblem: For their blazon, an idea would be to have a clean shield divided vertically straight down the middle—half black, half white (per pale). Inspired by the balance of Yin and Yang, this design carries a strong double meaning:

-- Impartiality & Mediation: standing for neutrality, fairness, and the ability to listen to both sides without bias.

-- Presence & Discretion: balancing welcoming warmth in public (light) with quiet, discreet action behind the scenes (shadow) through silent reports and constructive feedback.

Visually, this sharp monochrome contrast ensures maximum readability on avatars, nameplates, or Discord badges, making it instantly recognizable even from a distance without looking like an overbearing official staff badge.
title: A new role to foster safety and welcoming spaces in-game: Community Stewards
